cf.title: Historic snapshot doesn't track txns committed in BUILDING_SNAPSHOT state

input.subject: Historic snapshot doesn't track txns committed in BUILDING_SNAPSHOT state

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: message #2 agrees this is a bug, and the fix adds no user-visible surface. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point about a separate list of catalog-marking WAL records in the BUILDING_SNAPSHOT path. The visible material does not show v4-0001, so it is unknown whether that point is already answered. What remains is a correctness judgment in the snapshot builder that needs a committer who knows logical decoding.

brief.title: Track transactions committed during BUILDING_SNAPSHOT in logical decoding
brief.problem: Logical decoding does not record transactions that commit while the snapshot builder is in BUILDING_SNAPSHOT state, because xact_decode() returns early before FULL_SNAPSHOT. A later transaction can then get a historic snapshot that misses a catalog change, and decoding fails with "could not map filenumber ... to relation OID". This breaks logical replication or slot creation for users who create a subscription or slot while other transactions run DDL.
brief.proposed_design: The patch makes decoding track transactions committed during BUILDING_SNAPSHOT so that later snapshots see their catalog changes. Since the historic snapshot tracks only catalog-modifying transactions, it also handles WAL records that may mark a transaction as catalog modifying during BUILDING_SNAPSHOT, namely XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID and XLOG_HEAP_INPLACE. A second patch adds an isolation test, snapshot_build, to contrib/test_decoding.
author_claims: The bug can make a transaction take an incorrect historic snapshot and stop logical replication.
The new snapshot_build test in test_decoding reproduces the scenario.
brief.thread_state: Michael Paquier agreed it is a bug, and Bertrand Drouvot backed the approach, reviewed v2 and v3, and found v3-0002 fine. Ajin Cherian asked why the patch calls ReorderBufferXidSetCatalogChanges instead of SnapBuildProcessNewCid, and the author points to v4-0001 in one of three parallel threads.
unclear: The visible material does not show v4-0001 or say how it answers Bertrand's v3 comments and Ajin's question.
The thread does not say which branches the fix should be back-patched to.
The thread does not say whether the extra WAL handling during BUILDING_SNAPSHOT adds measurable cost to slot creation.
v1 touched snapbuild.c and v3 does not, and the thread does not say why.
search_queries: could not map filenumber relation OID

objections.title: Hand-kept list of catalog-marking WAL records in the BUILDING_SNAPSHOT path
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds or changes a WAL record that marks a transaction as catalog modifying and updates the FULL_SNAPSHOT decode path only. Slots created while such transactions commit get a snapshot that misses the change. Users see the same "could not map filenumber" error, and no test or assertion catches the gap.
objections.argument: v3-0001 adds a second, state-specific branch in decode.c that handles only XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID and XLOG_HEAP_INPLACE, with the comment "Currently only XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID means a catalog modifying". Message #8 suggests routing BUILDING_SNAPSHOT through the existing record handlers, so that future changes there apply here too. Message #9 asks why the patch calls ReorderBufferXidSetCatalogChanges and does not use SnapBuildProcessNewCid. The visible material does not show that v4-0001 removes the duplicated list or answers either point.
objections.author_must_show: Does v4-0001 reuse the existing record handlers so that a new catalog-marking record is covered without a separate BUILDING_SNAPSHOT edit, and if not, what catches the omission?

critic.reasoning: Message #8 raises the same concern about the v3 branch in decode.c, and message #9 asks a related question. The author's reply points to v4-0001 in another thread, which the visible material does not show, so nothing here answers the point.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes how decode.c handles commit, XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID and XLOG_HEAP_INPLACE records before FULL_SNAPSHOT.

touch_points.reason: This is a bug fix in logical decoding, and the thread does not say which branches receive it.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")

questions: Does v4-0001 reuse the existing record handlers during BUILDING_SNAPSHOT, and if not, what catches a new catalog-marking record that is added only to the FULL_SNAPSHOT path?
Why does the patch call ReorderBufferXidSetCatalogChanges for XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID and not SnapBuildProcessNewCid, as message #9 asks?
Which of the three parallel threads holds the current patch, and can the review continue in one thread?
Which branches should receive the fix, and does the patch apply to them without changes that affect extensions?
Why did v1 change snapbuild.c while v3 changes only decode.c?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the snapshot builder and the reorder buffer in logical decoding. Masahiko Sawada is listed as a reviewer on the CommitFest entry but has not posted in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of historic snapshots built during slot creation on every branch that receives the fix. A mistake here causes decoding errors or wrong decoded data, with no time limit.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v1 to v4, answered reviewers, and moved the entry across CommitFests for more than two years, so the author is likely to stay for fixes.

priority.reason: The bug is agreed in message #2 and the patch is small, but the entry has been in 12 CommitFests with no committer posting on the design. The patch is small, but snapshot builder state changes need careful review, and the work is split across three threads.

provisional_note: The code and v4-0001 were not read, so the correctness of tracking commits before FULL_SNAPSHOT is not judged. It was also not checked whether snapshot files in pg_logical/snapshots, written by unfixed binaries, keep the bad state after a minor upgrade.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Global snapshots
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add Clock-SI based global snapshots to core: a new SLRU mapping xids to a physical-clock-based GlobalCSN, an InDoubt commit state, snapshot import/export and global prepare/assign SQL functions, and delayed oldestXmin advancement so snapshots can be shared across Postgres instances. postgres_fdw would use this infrastructure with a minimal 2PC to give cross-node transactions snapshot isolation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was rebased in November 2018, but the further work the author planned (including a line-by-line review by committers) did not happen before the commitfest closed. Andres Freund proposed marking it returned with feedback, and the author agreed, saying it would not realistically go in during the last commitfest and would be reopened in the next release cycle. Robert Haas had asked for further research on the design, but the visible messages show the entry was closed for lack of progress, not because of a decisive technical objection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This hasn't happened yet, so I think this ought to be marked ad returned
with feedback?

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid duplicate XIDs at recovery when building initial snapshot - take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reverts commit 1df21ddb, which dropped duplicate XIDs from XLOG_RUNNING_XACTS records only when a standby applies them. Instead, GetRunningTransactionData() sorts the XIDs and subxids and removes duplicates on the primary whenever it finds a dummy two-phase proc entry, so the WAL record never holds duplicates.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs voted against the patch because it removes duplicates while holding ProcArrayLock, which is already a bottleneck, and he asked for proof that the performance cost is negligible. He also judged the committed fix in 1df21ddb sufficient and said the new patch was too complex to backpatch. The author agreed with these concerns and marked the patch returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I hadn't realised this patch holds ProcArrayLock while removing duplicates.
Now I know I vote against applying this patch unless someone can show that
the performance effects of doing so are negligable, which I doubt.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a hot standby. It adds a catalog-table flag to existing WAL records so the standby can detect snapshot conflicts with logical slots, and it drops conflicting slots, including when wal_level on the primary drops below logical.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn. The last messages show the patch set needing repeated rebases and its TAP tests failing intermittently: Rahila Syed reported 018_standby_logical_decoding_xmins.pl failures, and Alvaro Herrera found 019_standby_logical_decoding_conflicts.pl timing out after a rebase in March 2020. No later reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: old_snapshot: add test for coverage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a regression test for the contrib/old_snapshot extension so that its code coverage goes from 0% to 100%. It is a standalone test inside the extension.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found that the test does not exercise the extension in a meaningful way. Daniel Gustafsson added that its LIMIT 0 could hide bugs behind a passing result. Tom Lane suggested testing old_snapshot through src/test/modules/snapshot_too_old instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking at this I agree, this test doesn't provide enough to be of value and
the LIMIT 0 might even hide bugs under a postive test result.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Craig Ringer (ringerc), Amit Khandekar (amitdkhan), Ibrar Ahmed (ibrar)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a physical standby, with catalog-row conflicts on the standby detected from the existing snapshot-conflict WAL records, which gain a flag marking catalog tables. It replaces an earlier design that periodically logged the primary's catalog xmin horizon, and leaves hot_standby_feedback optional.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry died of inactivity. In March 2020 Alvaro Herrera rebased the patch, and its new conflict test then timed out and stopped the test run. No updated version followed, so after six months without updates Michael Paquier returned it with feedback, noting that the patch no longer applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No updates in the last six months, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: XLog size reductions: Reduced XLog record header size
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patchset makes the WAL record header variable-length, which shrinks it to 14-21 bytes, with about 4-5% less WAL estimated for pgbench. It varlength-encodes the record length, gives rmgrs their own info byte, includes the XID only when the record asks for it with XLOG_INCLUDE_XID, and adds an invalid rmgr ID 0 used to detect the end of WAL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after review. Michael Paquier objected to the opt-in XLOG_INCLUDE_XID interface and questioned the use of rmgr ID 0 as an end-of-WAL marker. Pavel Borisov then asked for benchmarks showing the gain was large enough, the benchmarking was still a todo, and a reminder from Andrey M. Borodin in April 2024 got no visible reply before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But at the second round, some doubt arises on whether this long
patchset indeed introduces enough performance gain?

precedents_retrieved.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zheng Li (zhengli), Zhijie Hou (houzj), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), vigneshwaran C (vignesh.postgres), Runqi Tian (runqitian)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replicate DDL commands through logical replication so that schema changes reach subscribers, for example during major version upgrades. The later patch set deparses DDL commands in event triggers into a JSON format string, WAL-logs it, and the apply worker rebuilds and runs the command, starting with create, alter and drop table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert no-op changes to BufferGetPage()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert no-op changes to BufferGetPage()
precedents_retrieved.objection:
The reverted changes were intended to force a choice of whether any
newly-added BufferGetPage() calls needed to be accompanied by a
test of the snapshot age, to support the "snapshot too old"
feature.  Such an accompanying test is needed in about 7% of the
cases, where the page is being used as part of a scan rather than
positioning for other purposes (such as DML or vacuuming).  The
additional effort required for back-patching, and the doubt whether
the intended benefit would really be there, have indicated it is
best just to rely on developers to do the right thing based on
comments and existing usage, as we do with many other conventions.

This change should have little or no effect on generated executable
code.

Motivated by the back-patching pain of Tom Lane and Robert Haas

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at this fix. Message #10 points to three parallel threads on this bug, with v4-0001 in one of them, but the material does not show those threads or any rejection reason from them.

This is an internal bug fix in logical decoding with no user-facing surface. It adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql change or dump content, so nothing is left for a standards or compatibility objection to rest on. Back-patch scope and any change in which transactions get decoded right after slot creation could not be checked without v4-0001.

The fix changes in-memory snapshot builder state in decode.c and adds no WAL record, catalog, wire or ABI change. One point could not be checked: whether snapshot files already in pg_logical/snapshots, written by unfixed binaries, keep the bad state after a minor upgrade.

The proposal fixes a correctness bug inside logical decoding's snapshot builder and adds a test. It does not change who can create slots or subscriptions, adds no privilege, role, setting or interface, and exposes no new data, so there is no security or privilege aspect to object to.

The fix is desirable, and its cost falls only on decoding during slot creation. From this angle the only concern is the duplicated record list. Committability: Masahiko Sawada is listed as a reviewer, but no committer shows engagement in the visible thread, and the work is split across three threads.

This is a bug fix in decode.c for an error users should never see, as message #2 says. Postgres has no existing feature, option, extension or external tool that avoids the wrong historic snapshot, so nothing from the already-exists angle applies.

This is a bug fix for a user-visible error ("could not map filenumber ... to relation OID") that stops logical replication when a slot or subscription is created during concurrent DDL. A committer agreed it must be fixed (message #2), so demand is not the open question.
